payload.name: Preserve compound topics during memory extraction
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists multiple topics or items (e.g., 'A and B', 'A, B, and C'), include all named items when creating a memory from that message; do not drop any element during summarization or paraphrase.
content: During extraction, when the speaker explicitly names multiple topics or items (e.g., 'dreams and life', 'A, B, and C'), preserve every named item in the memory candidate content; do not paraphrase or merge them into a single broader term.
If the final memory content omits any item that the source message explicitly listed, revise the candidate (or issue an UPDATE) so the memory retains the full set.

solves: The extraction summarized 'dreams and life' as 'reflecting on life', dropping an explicitly named element, so the memory partially covered the claim. Compound phrases are paraphrased too aggressively during candidate generation, losing items. This rule applies whenever a message enumerates multiple topics that a memory should retain.
